notes:
Account snapshot: mid-market search platform focused on enterprise document search and reranking. Engaged July 2025 through an AE intro; AE Jordan Blake + SE Priya Nair ran a 6-week evaluation/POC. Primary ask: replace legacy reranker with Redwood-hosted models for better relevance and to add streaming for interactive search sessions.

Key technical requirements: target p95 <= 150ms for chat-like search interactions, sustained 120 qps for simple queries with 8 concurrent streaming sessions, ability to pin model versions, audit logs + KMS integration, adherence to regional data residency (NA) for a subset of customers.

POC timeline (high level):
- 2025-08-20: Intro call (AE) - request for low-latency streaming demo, gave workload traces.
- 2025-09-03: SE deep-dive - shared request distribution and 95th percentile targets; Redwood suggested batching + KV cache.
- 2025-09-15: Live demo (ff_2025-09-15_01) - streaming demo looked good in isolated tests.
- 2025-10-03: Load test (customer-run) - observed p95 ~420ms at 8 concurrent streams; streaming stalls ~2-4s intermittently for long responses (see /drive/perf-reports/sq-loadtest-2025-10-03.html).
- 2025-10-07: Redwood perf follow-up with kernel/quant suggestions (ff_2025-10-07_perf_demo). SE recommended Dedicated pool and reduced sequence-length quant profile; engineering asked for a migration POC.
- 2025-10-21: Security review kickoff - customer asked for SOC2 evidence, KMS flow diagram, audit log retention policy.
- 2025-11-12: Customer ran competitor PoC (on-prem optimized runtime) and reported consistent p95 ~120-160ms; this shifted bias.
- 2025-11-20: Internal budget freeze declared for new infra until FY26 planning; champion (VP Eng) left company.
- 2025-12-01: Final call - customer says "we can't justify switching while budget & champion are gone" and moves to pause.

What we tried: focused perf tuning (suggested KV caching + request routing to lower-latency model variant), offered Dedicated reserved GPUs for predictable throughput and a short-term credit to run a Redwood-managed stress test. SE ran profiling and found that most p95 spikes came from streaming re-assembly overhead on small packets and from inefficient kernel selection at seq-len 2048. Proposed mitigations: smaller chunking, prefix cache, and kernel override for relevant model family.

Customer feedback (direct quotes):
- "Great team, results promising in isolation, but at scale we hit stalls that break our UX." (Lead Eng)
- "Our procurement now wants hard SLAs; the on-prem option from Vendor X met our latency bar in their demo." (CTO)

Reasons for stall / closed-lost dynamics:
- Technical: p95 SLO not met under real concurrency; streaming stalls unacceptable for their interactive product.
- Commercial: competitor showcased lower-latency on-prem PoC and procurement favored their price/perf given current budget constraints.
- Organizational: internal champion left and new stakeholders deprioritized migration.

Next steps / playbook: archive as lost-for-now; keep quarterly check-ins on product perf improvements (target Q2 2026 kernel/streaming optimizer release). If customer unfreezes budget or VP level champion returns, request a 2-week Redwood-managed Dedicated PoC with explicit load profile and agreed success metrics (p95 < 180ms sustained, streaming latency < 250ms inter-token).

Action items left open:
- RDW-1127: produce KMS integration diagram for security team (pending).
- RDW-1184: export of load test traces + our annotated perf analysis (delivered, awaiting review).
- Follow-up tickler: AE to schedule re-engage for 2026-04 (if budget calendar reopens).

Sales notes: keep in 'stalled' bucket; add competitor loss reason; mark as high-opportunity if dedicated/priv infra budget opens.
